stories.headline: Cowboys' Texas-themed jabs at Houston tops Week 4 trolls
stories.summary: The calendar shifted to October, and the trolls are becoming a little more impactful, led by the Dallas Cowboys.
stories.body:
Welcome to the first weekend of October, when the games get a little more meaningful and the trolls follow suit. Week 4 of the NFL season proved exactly that.

The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Houston Texans 34-30 on the road. Facing a four-point deficit with 2:23 left, Dallas went on an 11-play, 74-yard drive that concluded with a 12-yard touchdown catch by wide receiver CeeDee Lamb.

It put the Cowboys up for good and capped a stellar performance from Lamb. He had a whopping 17 catches -- second most in franchise history -- for 189 yards. It's the most receptions by any player since Keenan Allen had 18 in Week 3 of the 2023 season, according to ESPN Research.

Dallas had clever jabs lined up for the in-state matchup. The Cowboys referenced country star Ella Langley's hit track, "Choosin' Texas," in a social media post, adding "Dallas" ahead of "Texas."

Then, Dallas put a spin on the opening sequence from the sitcom "King of the Hill," which is set in Texas. The illustration featured Lamb, Dak Prescott, wide receiver George Pickens and safety Caleb Downs hanging out together with "Kings of the State" written above them.

Here are the other top trolls from Week 4.

Carolina Panthers 32, Detroit Lions 26
It required one final stop, but the Panthers survived for a "Sunday Night Football" win against the Lions.

Carolina held a six-point lead when Detroit regained possession with 2:06 left in the game. Four plays later, the Lions turned it over on downs, clinching the Panthers' victory. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns -- both to wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan, who had 14 catches for 192 yards. Their teammate, running back Chuba Hubbard, added 122 yards on the ground and two scores.

Carolina understood the assignment postgame when poking fun at Detroit. It shared an image of a Panther standing on a ledge and growling over a lion, writing in the caption: "The Lion's King."

Seattle Seahawks 30, Los Angeles Chargers 23
Seattle held on to beat Los Angeles in a bounce-back victory.

The Chargers had a chance to tie the score with 1:42 remaining, but the Seahawks sacked quarterback Justin Herbert to force a fumble, which they recovered to secure the win. Seattle forced four turnovers -- three came from Herbert and two led to touchdowns.

The Seahawks had multiple lightning- and charging-related trolls after the win.

Their first post was simple with the caption: "Lights Out," a reference to the nickname of Chargers legend Shawne Merriman. Seattle's victory comic included a robot out of charge. Seahawks defensive end Leonard Williams was labeled "The Lightning Thief," the title of a popular Rick Riordan novel. Then there was an image of a charging cord with tattered wires, captioned "0% battery," and another of a charging error with safety Nick Emmanwori sacking Herbert in the background.

Los Angeles Rams 24, Philadelphia Eagles 20
Los Angeles stormed back late to beat Philadelphia on the road.

The Rams outscored the Eagles 14-0 in the second half. The winning touchdown came on a 7-yard run by Kyren Williams with 1:10 left. The Eagles then had a turnover on downs, giving the Rams the ball and the win.

Even though the result was still up in the air, Los Angeles soft launched its troll with a post earlier in the day. The Rams shared an image of their players with "Rams in Philadelphia" written above them in a font evoking the hit comedy "Abbott Elementary," which is set in Philadelphia.

Just over five hours later, Los Angeles posted a test paper with scantron bubbles filled in to spell out "W."

San Francisco 49ers 24, Denver Broncos 14
The 49ers remain undefeated following a win against the Broncos.

San Francisco's defense shined, allowing just one touchdown and 296 total yards to Denver. The 49ers' offense played its part, too, specifically the offensive line -- the team has yet to give up a sack this season. The Niners are the first team to allow zero sacks through four games since the 2005 Indianapolis Colts, according to ESPN Research.

The Broncos' home stadium is Empower Field at Mile High, and even though the 49ers won at home, they highlighted the "mile high" component with a jab.

Jacksonville Jaguars 22, Cincinnati Bengals 17
Jacksonville's wire-to-wire win over Cincinnati prompted a simple, yet effective, troll.

Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence had 223 passing yards and one score, and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow threw for 428 yards, one touchdown plus two interceptions. Cincinnati put up a whopping 437 yards of offense but had only two touchdowns to show for it.

In a battle between Jaguars and Bengals, Jacksonville highlighted its win by writing "Jungle Cats" in its postgame caption.

Cleveland Browns 27, Pittsburgh Steelers 24
The Browns have won three straight games for the first time since 2023 after defeating the Steelers on "Thursday Night Football."

Pittsburgh tied the score with 1:42 remaining, but Cleveland responded by kicking a winning field goal with 10 ticks left. As a result, Deshaun Watson became the second Browns quarterback since 1970 to lead three straight winning drives in the fourth quarter or overtime, according to ESPN Research.

At first glance, Cleveland's Minecraft-themed post after the win seemed something ordinary. But it was a reference to former Pittsburgh head coach Mike Tomlin revealing his Minecraft world Wednesday. The Browns capitalized on the moment by building out an "L" in Minecraft blocks and writing: "Pittsburgh was defeated by the Dawg Pound."

stories.headline: Samoskevich scores twice and Kraken beat Flames 6-1 in home opener as Calgary stays winless
stories.summary: — Berkly Catton, Mackie Samoskevich and Bobby McMann scored within the first eight minutes of the game and the Seattle Kraken cruised to a 6-1 win over the Calgary Flames on Sunday night.
stories.body:
SEATTLE -- — Berkly Catton, Mackie Samoskevich and Bobby McMann scored within the first eight minutes of the game and the Seattle Kraken cruised to a 6-1 win over the Calgary Flames on Sunday night.


Samoskevich added another goal late in the second period and Joey Daccord made 32 saves. Shane Wright and Jordan Eberle also scored in Seattle's home opener.


Morgan Frost scored on the power play and Dustin Wolf stopped 21 shots for the Flames, who remain winless.


Catton opened the scoring 2:22 into the first period and Samoskevich scored at 4:40. It was Samoskevich’s first goal with Seattle after being acquired from the Florida Panthers in exchange for a 2026 first-round pick and a 2027 conditional second-round pick in June.


McMann gave the Kraken a three-goal lead 7:40 into the first, and Wright added another goal with 8:02 remaining in the second.


Frost spoiled Daccord’s shutout bid by scoring with 5:35 left in the game. It was the first power-play goal conceded by the Kraken this season. Eberle scored 39 seconds later.


Seattle is 2-1-0 after beating Calgary for the second time this season. In Thursday's win over the Flames, six different skaters scored to boost the Kraken.


Wolf has now surrendered 12 goals in his first two starts, both against Seattle. He averaged 3.01 goals against and had an .899 save percentage last season, and was a finalist for the Calder Memorial Trophy as top rookie for the 2024-25 season.


The Kraken and Flames meet once more this month on Oct. 30.


Up next
Kraken: Host the Vegas Golden Knights on Tuesday night.


Flames: Host the Colorado Avalanche on Thursday night.

stories.headline: 'Understanding': Swans dismiss talk of rift with Nick Blakey
stories.summary: Sydney list boss Chris Keane has played down talk of a rift with Nick Blakey, declaring the Swans are confident the defender will remain at the AFL club.
stories.body:
Sydney is adamant Nick Blakey will stay as the embattled AFL club prepares to reintegrate its five exiled players.

Blakey was one of five players who served a club-imposed ban through finals for breaching the Swans' behavioural standards at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne.

Swans vice-captain Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon were also stood down from round 24 to the club's preliminary final loss to Fremantle.

All five players are contracted for next year, with defender Blakey signed to the club until 2031 on a deal reportedly worth more than $1 million per season.

Blakey has been linked to a move back to his Victorian home after a report in The Age last month suggested his relationship with the Swans had deteriorated to the point where he had told associates he wanted to be traded.

But Swans list boss Chris Keane dismissed the speculation on Monday, declaring the club was confident of retaining Blakey.

Keane denied there had been tension between Blakey and the club.

"Nick's actually been really good through this whole process and understanding of the club's decision," he told reporters.

"The last couple of months have been challenging on a lot of different fronts, but Nick's been really good and understanding of the club's position.

"We've had no indication from Nick or his management that he's keen to explore anything, so we're really confident that he'll be at our footy club next year."

Keane wouldn't be drawn on whether the Swans would consider a trade if requested by Blakey.

"I can understand the interest at this time of year, but ... we're really dealing in hypotheticals at the moment," Keane said.

The five players had since returned to club headquarters after their suspension and individually offered apologies to colleagues and teammates.

Warner and Jordon come off contract at the end of 2027, while Heeney and Bice are signed until the end of 2028.

Heeney was crowned the club's best and fairest player last week and, in a two-minute pre-recorded video, expressed his determination to continue his playing career at Sydney.

"We've been in constant discussion with their managers mainly, but also with the players as well," Keane said.

"Them getting reintroduced into the club a couple of weeks ago was a good step forward and something that was necessary."

After heavily courting Western Australian product Warner last season, West Coast list boss Matt Clarke said the Eagles would not be in pursuit of the midfielder this trade period.

"Things are pretty clear where Chad sits for next year," Clarke said.

"He'll be at the Swans next year."

Keane added that the Swans are expecting a quiet trade period, outside of key forward Joel Amartey's move to Carlton.

Amartey's switch as an unrestricted free agent was confirmed on Friday, with a second-round pick - currently No.36 - coming back to the Swans.

"This year was more around retention," Keane said.

stories.headline: Lacob lauds Williams as world's best after Valkyries' Game 1 win
stories.summary: Gabby Williams scored 25 points and played lockdown defense in a performance that led Valkyries owner Joe Lacob to declare her the "best player in the world."
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Golden State Valkyries owner Joe Lacob walked through the tunnels of Chase Center following the Valkyries' 71-60 win over the Las Vegas Aces in Game 1 of the WNBA semifinals with a message he wanted to get off of his chest.

"Print this: Gabby Williams is the best player in the world," Lacob told ESPN.

Williams scored a team-high 25 points Sunday afternoon and scored or assisted on 36 of the Valkyries' points. On the other end, she held the Aces to just 29% on 4-of-14 shooting as the primary defender. Williams, who also had 11 rebounds and five assists, became the second player with 25 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a playoff game against the Aces. She is also the first Valkyries player to have a 25-10-5 playoff game.

After arriving in Golden State during the offseason, Williams has taken her play to another level with the Valkyries -- finishing second in Defensive Player of the Year voting and also adding to her offensive game. So far, she's averaging 25 points during the playoffs, which is the third-highest scoring average of the postseason. Only Wilson and Arike Ogunbowale have scored more.

Early in the game Sunday, Williams felt that the Aces were trying to make her uncomfortable, throwing a mixture of coverages at her. That's when she made sure she was intentional about getting everyone else involved.

"There are five players on the court," Williams said. "We were running really well in transition, so I found [Kayla Thornton] a couple times, and things started to open up on their own."

The Valkyries' ability to get out and run was fueled by their performance on the boards. Golden State outrebounded Las Vegas 52-25 -- the second-largest difference by any team in a playoff game in WNBA history. It also held the Aces to a season low in scoring.

The Aces made pushes, clawing back from down by as much as 11, but they never took away Golden State's momentum and couldn't get their deficit below five points down the stretch of the game.

"All we talked about the last 48 hours was rebounding and blocking them out, and we did not do that. Period," Aces coach Becky Hammon said. "The good news is, we played like ass and only lost by 10."

A'ja Wilson finished with 24 points on 8-of-21 field goal shooting and went 8-of-11 from the free throw line. Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young combined for 25 points.

"I've competed against A'ja my entire career, and she will go down in history as the best player to ever do it," Williams said. "This is what you dream about. You dream to play against players like that. Going up against them is all I care about. ... I just want to win."

Williams rolled her eyes when she heard what Lacob said about her, but the belief he has poured into her is the reason she is leading the Valkyries in their playoff push. During every game, she seeks out a fist bump from the owner to "absorb" some of his energy. When she watches replays of the game, she zooms in to see his spirited reaction to big plays.

"There she is," Lacob yelled when he saw Williams standing in the hallway after the game, his arms open for a hug. "Best player in the world. No one is saying it, but they need to start saying it."

stories.headline: Bahrain GP was the worst indictment of F1's new engine regs yet
stories.summary: There was a lot to love about Sunday's race. But it will forever be overshadowed by the mess caused by the new F1 engines.
stories.body:
SEPANG, Malaysia -- The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia already had a farcical name. Formula 1's unnecessarily complicated hybrid engines ensured the race will be remembered as one of the biggest farces in the sport's recent history.

F1's current engines, which feature a near 50-50 split between internal combustion energy and electrical battery elements, are already considered the biggest mistake the sport has made in recent times. Whenever they are consigned to the scrapheap, the foremost memories will be of Sunday's two formation laps in the rain.

"LOL, look at this," was all a laughing Max Verstappen could say over the radio as his Red Bull approached a handful of cars whose engines had simply shut down. His car had already done the same at the front of the pack a couple of minutes earlier.

It was an apt use of modern day slang: Laugh out loud was all you could really do. Collectively, and due to a perfect storm of circumstances, F1's cars had all ground to a walking speed, one after the other. The first attempt at starting the race -- already delayed 40 minutes, because these F1 cars cannot race in extremely wet conditions -- was aborted, with another wait to allow the 11 teams to download and implement a software update from the governing FIA.

"Horrible," said reigning world champion Lando Norris after the race. "It just proves that we shouldn't have any of that stuff on the electronic side".

George Russell, who also dealt with a heartbreaking late engine failure which has all but handed Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli the 2026 championship, said, "The whole day was a bit of a faff. It didn't feel very F1 today".

Carlos Sainz summed up the situation best of all: "I think F1 needs to have a hard look at themselves and see how we ended up in this situation."

There's a lot to still love about F1 in 2026, and some of it was on show towards the end of Sunday's chaotic race. But the absolute worst of the sport was also showcased in brutal fashion before a competitive lap had even been completed.

What exactly happened?
As well as new-look cars and new V6 turbo hybrid engines, this year introduced a new set of Pirelli tyres. The Italian company's wet-weather tyres have been a question-mark all season, however: bar a February test behind closed doors in Spain and wet-weather tests for Red Bull, Racing Bulls and Ferrari earlier in the year, no teams had done any meaningful runs on the intermediate or full wets prior to this weekend.

The FIA immediately delayed the start as the weather intensified, with a nearby thunderstorm also complicating things. Several teams briefly lost their weather radars on the pit wall, while some of the marshal panels lining the circuit briefly stopped working.

At 3:40 p.m. local time, 40 minutes after the race was supposed to start, the FIA attempted to get things underway with two formation laps behind the safety car, followed by a standing start from the grid. The rain had started easing off and the track was wet, but it looked as though race control was going to make a go of it. But those formation laps were always going to be an exercise in extreme caution.

Several corners into the first formation lap is where things started going wrong, when the cars encountered a software bug baked into the algorithms that dictate F1's new complicated engines. During rain, for safety reasons, engine modes run at a maximum deployment of 250 kilowatts of deployment in certain sectors, down from 350kW in dry conditions. Once Verstappen, leading the pack but tiptoeing around on the cold intermediates, dropped below a speed of 50 km/h, the algorithms dictating the behaviour of his engine started having problems: essentially, the MGU-K no longer kicked in to feed power into his low-revving engine. The restriction on the car's hybrid-electric component is meant to prevent teams from effectively using it as a traction control device at the start of a race; this time, however, the combination of not running on wet tires with an extremely wet tarmac meant drivers were applying much less throttle than normal.

The algorithm did not spot the difference, so kicked in. With the additional power boost locked out, the internal combustion engine was effectively dying without a surge of recovery power from the electrical side.

You wouldn't be the only one confused by this: F1 drivers have said this year's debriefs with engineers are longer and more complicated than ever. Many have spoken about their engines behaving in radically different ways lap to lap, as self-learning algorithms kick in power at different points.

In the moment, what was happening was unclear: Some thought Verstappen simply had an engine issue.

"There was nothing going on," he said later. "That was the problem. It was just like driving at, what, 35 km/h, going uphill, actually losing speed. So, yeah, I don't know exactly, because when you go too low in speed and too low RPM, for whatever reason, then it just bogs down. Normally it takes one or two seconds and it comes back."

But this time, the power did not come back. Verstappen's car was slowing so dramatically, which meant the cars behind him bunched up. But the rules state you cannot overtake the car in front on a formation lap.

"I triggered it first and then I look in my mirror, I just see... I was like, "Wait, are they waiting for me or what's going on...?" Verstappen said.

Those behind were, in fact, waiting. The same thing happened to Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari, in second position, shortly after his car also dropped below the all-important 50 km/h benchmark.

"It was like the Lego race," Hamilton joked later, referring to the viral pre-race spectacle during the Miami Grand Prix in May.

While Verstappen somehow managed to avoid coming to a complete standstill, Hamilton's ground to a halt. The seven-time world champion had to restart his Ferrari's power unit on the pit straight. But unlike with Verstappen, cars slowly started passing Hamilton as he plummeted down the order.

"It was insane," said current championship leader Antonelli. "At some point we were five-wide in the straight, because we couldn't understand what was going on."

Hamilton's Ferrari seemed to suffer the most extreme version of the engine issue: By the time he did stop completely, he was half way down the order, and Audi, Williams, Racing Bulls and other teams' cars were facing similar issues around him. It was this scene a laughing Verstappen would later drive past. The start procedure was canceled, effectively a red flag.

And here is where the lack of wet tire usage this year had caught the FIA out.

"We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked, because there's been very little wet running this year," the governing body's single seater chief Nikolas Tombazis explained in a rare trip to the media pen after the race.

"There was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in. Basically, [on] the formation lap, some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely. That bug prevented the power from being redeployed, and for the cars to start again. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time, and not have such a situation.

"Once the problem happened, our guys realised very quickly what was happening, and had to work under a lot of time pressure for an update to the software, which was issued to the teams, and the teams had to install it on their cars.

The FIA later gave a simpler statement on what had happened, blaming a perfect storm of various factors. The governing body said "an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit's sector configuration led to an unintended loss of power for a number of cars".

The remedy was a software update -- code Tombazis admitted was a "cobbled up, hurried solution." Rewriting and sending the new code to the teams to install in their systems led to another delay. It meant the worst of the rain also disappeared, we got only a handful of laps on the intermediates and the prospect of a genuine wet-weather classic disappeared.

If you still need another way to think about it: The 11 teams competing in the pinnacle of motorsport hit Ctrl+Alt+Delete and installed a software update to race safely again.

The fallout
The FIA did apologize afterward for the chaos.

"All of that took about 20 minutes," Tombazis said. "It may have felt like five hours for spectators waiting in a race and for everybody else, which is understandable. And we are sorry about that. But I think it was quite a fast reaction given the problem."

The sport's governing body could easily direct critics toward a race ultimately full of incidents and overtaking. And, fair enough: Sepang was an entertaining spectacle.

Verstappen returned to the top step for the first time this season. Hamilton turned in a supreme drive for third after gambling incorrectly on slick tires over intermediates, which had him over a minute down on the lead early. Antonelli now looks certain to become the sport's youngest ever champion after Russell's late DNF (and the engine penalties likely to come with it).

It was a fitting return for the brilliant Sepang circuit, too. Yet, the engines are such a step in the wrong direction it's hard to look past it.

"That's what happens when you have these engines," Verstappen said. He's been outspoken about the regs since the first time he drove a 2026 car, so it's perhaps not a surprise what he said next.

"With a V8 you don't have these problems".

F1's current rules were drawn up over a period of years, and the promise of the V6 turbo hybrid engines was making the sport more appealing to new manufacturers -- Audi this year, General Motors by the end of the decade. But the price to lure two new manufacturers to the sport does not seem worth it so far.

F1 will make small tweaks to the engines over the next two years, shifting the 50-50 split closer towards a 60-40 split in favor of conventional combustion power over the electrical elements by 2028. But many in the paddock believe it will not be enough to make racing feel normal again.

Sainz, who has been vocal about the situation, believes the sport has to learn from Sepang. "It is clear the regs are extremely complicated for the drivers, for the teams, for the PUs, for the manufacturers," he said after the race. "Again, my only question mark is: Who, five years ago, decided that this was the direction to go?

"The FIA and F1 are doing the best they can with what was decided four or five years ago, but clearly what was decided four or five years ago is wrong."

A silver lining to end on: Sunday's engine farce may end up accelerating the push to drop V6s in favour of V8s at the earliest possible opportunity.

Whenever that day is, it cannot be soon enough.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal among clubs chasing winger Yildiz
stories.summary: Arsenal, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich are all chasing Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Arsenal, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich are all chasing Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz. Plus, could Endrick leave Real Madrid for AC Milan?

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are pushing for Kenan Yildiz with Arsenal and Bayern Munich also looking at the Juventus winger, reports Corriere dello Sport. Juve have been demanding at least €100 million for the 21-year-old for a year, but Madrid are reigniting their interest in him with the view to a move in the summer. They would want to pit him and Vinícius Júnior against each other, while Arsenal see the Turkiye international as the answer to their lack of options on the left and Bayern have been watching him from afar since his departure.

- AC Milan are planning to make another attempt to sign Real Madrid striker Endrick after being unable to bring him in during the summer, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. Madrid boss Jose Mourinho had initially refused to let the 20-year-old leave, but he has made just one substitute appearance this season that lasted four minutes. Milan's main competition from within Italy for the Brazil international is Roma, while Aston Villa were also unsuccessful in their efforts to bring him in last summer.

- Barcelona are willing to let Alejandro Balde leave on loan in January with Manchester United among the clubs interested in the left-back, according to TEAMtalk. The 22-year-old has fallen down the pecking order in Hansi Flick's squad and has only got onto the pitch once so far this season, playing the last 12 minutes in a 7-2 win over Racing Santander. The Spaniard's camp and intermediaries are already working hard to find a solution for him, while the Blaugrana could look to bring in a new left-back in 2027.

- Liverpool center back Giovanni Leoni is the latest name La Gazzetta dello Sport have linked with Juventus, as I Bianconeri aim to introduce young Italian talent to their squad. The Serie A side have turned their attention away from the likes of Arsenal's Riccardo Calafiori and Chelsea's Marco Palestra, who are now seen as unattainable, and had already made enquiries about a loan for Leoni in recent months. Liverpool haven't opened the door to the 19-year-old leaving, but Juventus aren't giving up on him.

- Barcelona are interested in 18-year-old FC Twente center back Ruud Nijstad, reports transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano. They are monitoring the young Dutchman, having already made contact about him in August but ultimately being told that a transfer wasn't possible as Twente wanted him to be a key player for them. More clubs are showing an interest in Nijstad and have started travelling to scout him.

- Real Madrid are among the clubs who could move to sign Manchester United attacker JJ Gabriel, according to Spanish newspaper AS. Various clubs across Europe are looking at the 15-year-old after it was made clear that he wants to leave the Red Devils and requested a transfer. Bayern Munich have emerged as major rivals for his signature and Barcelona have gained momentum in recent days. Man United have leaked that they will take legal action against any club that negotiates with Gabriel.

Other rumors
- Arsenal, Barcelona, AC Milan, and Juventus all want to sign 15-year-old Borussia Dortmund midfielder Justin Ejodamen. (TEAMtalk)

- Tottenham Hotspur have no interest in letting Micky van de Ven leave as Liverpool prepare to move for the centre-back next year. (Football Insider)

- Manchester United, Arsenal, and Chelsea are making regular checks on Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic. (Caught Offside)

- Newcastle United are open to letting 27-year-old midfielder Joe Willock leave in January. (Football Insider)

- Leeds United aren't planning on letting Dan James leave, but the 28-year-old could look to depart in January. (Football Insider)

- Roma are planning a contract extension for Mario Hermoso. (Nicolo Schira)

stories.headline: UFC 332 takeaways: Talbott, Silva validate their top billing
stories.summary: Payton Talbott finished another former champion in Deiveson Figueiredo on a night full of knockouts at UFC 332.
stories.body:
The options were plenty for performance bonuses after UFC 332 in Salt Lake City. The fight card set a UFC record for knockouts with 11, and nine came in the first round. The most resounding KO went to men's bantamweight Payton Talbott in the co-main event. He came out strong, sending former champion Deiveson Figueiredo to the canvas twice before finishing him a little over two minutes into the fight. The win is Talbott's second in a row over a former champion and likely means big things ahead for him, but the loss for Figueiredo doesn't do anything to minimize his legacy in the UFC.

The main event, which received prefight chatter over whether it was worthy of a headlining slot, was high energy but mostly one-sided. Natalia Silva, the No. 1 women's flyweight contender, earned her first UFC championship with a unanimous decision over Wang Cong. The 29-year-old joins men's flyweight Joshua Van as the only UFC champions under 30.

Was the main event criticism validated?
The UFC took heat on social media for booking Silva vs. Wang in a main event on a numbered card. Silva was at the front of a long line of women's flyweight title contenders, no question, but it's fair to say Wang, unranked by ESPN and outside the top five in the UFC's own rankings, jumped the queue.

But while I'm on board with a lot of the criticism the UFC receives for its matchmaking, especially at a championship level, I understand what the fight promotion was going for in this case: The UFC was trying to set up a couple of possible storylines involving Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the women's flyweight title to make the Silva-Wang title fight a possibility after suffering an undisclosed injury that will sideline her for "up to one year."

Why Wang? She might not have an extensive UFC résumé, but she beat Shevchenko in a kickboxing match in 2015. Their history is not unlike that of Alex Pereira and Israel Adesanya, who met twice in kickboxing, with Pereira winning both and knocking out Adesanya in one of those fights. It provided a setup for their UFC rivalry.

A Wang vs. Shevchenko angle became moot, as things turned out, because Silva was too much for the Chinese fighter to handle. Wang came in with a 10-1 MMA record, but she had zero fights against top-10 flyweights, and it showed. Silva, by contrast, came in having defeated former UFC champions (Jessica Andrade, Alexa Grasso and Rose Namajunas) in each of her past three fights.

Silva was too fast, too elusive and too precise with her punches and kicks. Wang had no answers, looked lost and couldn't get her offense going until the fifth round, when it was too late. Not to vindicate the prefight matchmaking criticism, but this sure was a lopsided and not-so-fiery bout, one that got booed by a crowd that had been treated to a UFC-record 11 knockouts on the night.

So now the 125-pound division is left with the Silva vs. Shevchenko storyline we were expecting to see before Shevchenko was injured. It will be interesting to see how Silva's speed holds up when she meets her predecessor with the belt, and how differently she'll fight when up against an opponent with a strong grappling game. Oddly, that wasn't even addressed in Silva's postfight interview in the cage. Shevchenko's name wasn't even mentioned. Now, that is a UFC decision worth questioning. -- Jeff Wagenheim

Quick thanks to Figueiredo

MMA loves to move quickly, and it's ready to move very fast with Talbott. Talbott is everything MMA could want in a prospect, and his future is very bright.

So before we all take off on the Talbott train (as we inevitably will), let's take a moment to shout out one of the most exciting flyweights of all time, Figueiredo.

Let's be honest, Figueiredo was always a borrowed bantamweight. He struggled to make 125 pounds, and most of the sport was happy to see him ditch the weight cut in 2023, but he was also undersized at 135.

It's easy to forget now, as UFC men's flyweight champion Van has taken the sport by storm -- but the flyweight division was still in a precarious position when Figueiredo made his mark in 2020. Henry Cejudo saved the division by knocking out TJ Dillashaw in 2018, but then eventually vacated a weight class the UFC seriously considered shutting down. Figueiredo picked up where Cejudo left off, saving the division with his one-punch knockout power and (frankly) villain charisma. He played the role of "bad guy" in his back-to-back fights against Joseph Benavidez in 2020, as well as his four-fight rivalry with Brandon Moreno.

It was inevitable when he moved up in weight, but for a three-year period, Figueiredo was the exact figure the flyweight division needed. The 38-year-old's career is undoubtedly coming to an end soon, but Figueiredo was not just a terrific fighter and champion in his prime, he will forever be remembered as a significant hero of flyweight MMA. -- Brett Okamoto

stories.summary: Sam Walker is in line for an Australian Test debut as one of six debutants in Kevin Walters' World Cup squad.
stories.body:
Isaah Yeo will delay pectoral surgery to be captain for Australia's Rugby League World Cup campaign, after coach Kevin Walters unveiled a 23-man squad that includes Sydney Roosters halfback Sam Walker.

One of six debutants in the squad, Walker will be locked in a four-way battle with Cameron Munster, Tom Dearden and Mitchell Moses for a spot in the Kangaroos' halves.

Brisbane star Reece Walsh was also selected in Walters' squad and will compete with Clive Churchill medallist James Tedesco for the fullback role.

Latrell Mitchell has also returned to the Test team after battling injuries over recent seasons.

"I'm really happy with the balance of the squad," Walters said.

"We have some real strike power and a significant amount of experience, along with size, power and speed.

"This will be a huge test. I have never before seen the amount of talent spread across the top nations. We are going to need to be at our best to take out the World Cup."

Oct. 2: What to expect from Eagles without DeVonta Smith

By Matt Bowen

With reports that a hamstring injury will keep Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith out of the lineup this Sunday in the home matchup against the Rams, let's discuss the fantasy implications for Philadelphia.

If you're a Smith manager, you can pivot to Dontayvion Wicks or Makai Lemon as streaming options, as both are available in slightly more than 50% of ESPN leagues. You can also check out the last-minute pickups column for a handful of other viable options at wide receiver.

Wicks scored 12 or more points in each of his first two games, catching a touchdown in Week 1. He has a big-play element to his game (19.9 YPC), so he will see more vertical opportunities Sunday against a Rams defense that will mix man and zone coverages. He can be played as a WR3/flex with more upside due to the third-level targets (seven targets of 15 or more air yards this season).

Lemon has seen only nine targets on the season, catching seven of them for 38 yards. However, the rookie has run 28 routes per game and his role should expand versus L.A. Going back to Lemon's college tape at USC, he can manipulate coverage at the top of the route, plus he accelerates thorough the ball. Those are good traits to have in this league. He should be viewed as a lower-tier WR3 for this matchup.

Expect the Eagles to be more run-heavy in this game without Smith, which should put Saquon Barkley at 15-20 carries. Meanwhile, Jalen Hurts -- who was already outside of the top 10 QBs in our consensus ranks -- will have an even lower ceiling heading into Sunday. Yes, Hurts can provide a boost to the lineup due to his running ability, as he averages 29 yards per game, but he has scored only one rushing touchdown on the season.

Oct. 2: You should be paying attention to Aaron Rodgers

By Adam Rank

At least for one night in Cleveland, Aaron Rodgers turned back the clock. Was it the 299 passing yards? The three touchdowns? Or the fact that I really believed that his desperation heave in the waning seconds of the game was going to find its way into the mitts of a Steelers receiver who would carry it into the end zone for a walk-off touchdown?

Sure, all of it.

Look, I make no apologies for being the supporter of a team that was on the losing side of "Rodgers magic" way too many times. However, I'm not going to lie when I tell you I was seriously nervous on that final throw. I've seen it too many times.

The point is, Rodgers was very impressive for the second consecutive week. Although, the interception at the end, we could have done without. Still, another huge performance which raises the question: What do we do with Rodgers moving forward?

Patrick Mahomes and Bryce Young are on a bye next week. (Oh yeah, the bye weeks are getting ready to start!) A number of quarterbacks are missing this week and possibly next. But it goes a little bit beyond that. Like, what if some of the guys we believed in back in August continue to struggle? I'm looking at you, Justin Herbert and Drake Maye. Rodgers has a plus matchup next week against the Colts. Do you have the nerve to put him into your starting lineup?

Something to think about. Of course, most people have to wait until Tuesday to put in a waiver claim. And so many things can happen between now and then. But for the moment, Rodgers is looking like a borderline QB1 in fantasy circles, which is not something that I would have thought about six weeks ago. Heck, even two weeks ago.

While we're reassessing our preseason preconceptions ... my editor and I enjoyed some banter during the game, with the biggest question being, are the Browns a good football team? Does it matter? The schedule isn't overly daunting. The team you were likely picking against in your survivor league has now won three consecutive games. Are they good? That's up to interpretation. They are interesting.

Here are some other notes from the night.

Quinshon Judkins had his best game of the season, rushing for 53 yards and a touchdown. He also had six receptions for 43 yards on seven targets. Judkins had been a low-end RB2 with some upside for the first three games of the season. Daniel Dopp and I talked about this on "Fantasy Live" earlier this week. He was disappointing, but you're compelled to start him because, well, who else could you start? I would love to see him maintain some consistency in the passing game moving forward.
Denzel Boston had four receptions for 89 yards. I've been really impressed by him. He's got a tough matchup looming against the Jets next week. He's still pushing as a potential WR3.
Harold Fannin Jr. had three receptions for 27 yards and a touchdown. The touchdown salvaged his game this week. Maybe make plans for another option next week. The Jets have allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to tight ends this season heading into Week 4.
One other note about Rodgers. He was pushing the ball down the field. That was huge for DK Metcalf who finished with five receptions for 115 yards. If the Steelers can get this version of Rodgers and DK, they could be cooking.
Roman Wilson scored a touchdown for the second consecutive game. The first time that's happened in his career. I'm not making any waiver claims for him just yet. He's had six targets in each game this season. I need to see more snaps before I invest, but he's showing a lot of boom-or-bust potential. And again, he's one to keep an eye on as the bye weeks approach.

Are the Browns good? Is Aaron Rodgers for real? This game was more than what we could have asked for on a Thursday night.

Oct. 1: Saints place RB Etienne Jr. on IR

By Eric Moody

The New Orleans Saints placed RB Travis Etienne Jr. on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, meaning he'll miss at least four games. With New Orleans' Week 8 bye, the earliest he can return is Week 9. That leaves Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller in line for more work in the backfield.

Kamara should get the first chance at leading the backfield. Etienne had taken on the largest share of the workload in Week 3 and finished with 13 carries despite leaving in the third quarter, while Kamara had nine and Miller had four.

Kamara hasn't been very efficient this season (2.8 YPC), but more touches could put him back in the RB2 conversation. He should see plenty of carries and remain involved in the passing game, giving him a solid floor as a flex option.

Miller should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Double-digit touches are possible with Etienne out, but I'd keep him on the bench until we get a better idea of how New Orleans plans to split the work.

Don't forget about CJ Donaldson, either. Coach Kellen Moore gave him the Saints' first touch inside the 10-yard line last week. If that continues, Donaldson could have a role near the goal line, even if Kamara and Miller handle most of the work.

Kamara is the one I'd feel comfortable starting right away. Miller belongs on rosters in 12-team leagues, while Donaldson is more of a deeper league player to monitor.

Dolphins move towards split backfield to replace Achane

By Marcel Louis-Jacques

Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II was one of the most popular adds in fantasy this week. The former Doak Walker Award winner offers rare size for the position and handled a 20-touch workload in place of De'Von Achane in Week 3.

We all know opportunity is a premium commodity in fantasy, but it's important to remember that Gordon was the Dolphins' only other active running back last week. Jaylen Wright, the former fourth-round pick, has seldom seen the field during his three-year career but ran for 107 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries filling in for Achane against the Jets last season.

Wright offers sub-4.40 speed and a versatile skill set. Speaking to Wright and Gordon this week, they sound ready to share the workload moving forward.

Dolphins Coach Jeff Hafley envisions a split backfield, so expect them to ride with the hot hand.

Sept. 30: TNF injury updates, 10 trends to know for Week 4

By Michael F. Florio

Rico Dowdle did not practice to start the week and is out for the Pittsburgh Steelers' "Thursday Night Football" matchup with the Cleveland Browns. With Dowdle sidelined last week, Jaylen Warren handled the bulk of the opportunities, playing 90% of the snaps and garnering 17 carries and four targets. Warren finished with 176 total yards and 20.6 fantasy points (RB8).

Warren has a chance to build off of that in Cleveland, as the Browns have allowed the sixth-most yards on outside runs and have missed tackles at the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. Warren should be started over David Montgomery, Quinshon Judkins, Omarion Hampton, Rhamondre Stevenson and Jadarian Price.

Trends to know for Week 4

Defenses have altered the way they play Drake Maye since last season's playoffs. Teams are rushing four men -- or fewer, at times -- at a high rate against the New England Patriots but have still been able to create quick pressure. Last week, the Jacksonville Jaguars rushed four or fewer on 82% of dropbacks and still created pressure in under 2.5 seconds, on average. Each team has played Cover 6 at least 15% of the time against Maye.

Simply put, teams are able to get to Maye quickly without blitzing, meaning they are able to drop more players into coverage. Maye has to make quick decisions, and it is not allowing enough time for his receivers to consistently get open. It also has seemingly sped the clock up in his head.

I think Maye will eventually figure it out, and his value will likely never be lower, especially in dynasty leagues. These struggles create a trade-for opportunity. However, until we see Maye figure it out, it is very tough to trust him in redraft leagues.

Bryce Young faces a Detroit Lions defense that has allowed the most passing yards and the second-most touchdowns to QBs. Every QB to face Detroit has scored at least 23 fantasy points, and they've respectively finished QB8, QB1 and QB3.
Bhayshul Tuten has forced 15 missed tackles on outside runs (second most), and the Cincinnati Bengals have the sixth-highest rate of missed tackles on such runs (40%).
Bucky Irving, who has the fourth-most rushing yards on outside runs, faces the Green Bay Packers, who have allowed the most yards on those runs.
Rashee Rice had eight of his nine targets come against zone defense last week. The Las Vegas Raiders play zone 81% of the time.
Garrett Wilson has a 62% target share against man coverage, by far the highest in the NFL. He faces the Chicago Bears, who have played man at the fourth-highest rate.
DJ Moore has a 35% target share against man coverage, and the Patriots play man at the second-highest rate in the NFL.
Stefon Diggs has a team-high 30% target share against man coverage, which the Indianapolis Colts play at the third-highest rate in the league. The Colts also have allowed the most yards to slot receivers, and Diggs has lined up in the slot for 51% of his routes so far this season.
The Lions have allowed the most yards and touchdowns to tight ends. Darren Waller is coming off season highs in snap rate ( 51%) and targets (eight).
Cam Ward has 717 career dropbacks. Of QBs with that many in the Next Gen Stats era, he ranks last in yards per attempt (5.8) and success rate (36.5%). Only Zach Wilson (-0.25) has a lower EPA per dropback (-0.23).

Add Braelon Allen, stash Zach Charbonnet if you need RBs

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

How you doin', Vampire league managers?

Better yet, how about you zero-RB strategizers?

The 2026 season hasn't been the friendliest to those who went the cheap route at running back, at least not so far. Through three weeks, only two running backs selected outside the top 30 at the position on average have scored as many as 15 fantasy points in a game: Chuba Hubbard (twice) and Kyle Monangai. And anyone playing the Vampire format or going full zero-RB might not have even drafted either player, considering Hubbard went 34th and Monangai 37th; that'd be right around the four-running back average per team in the format.

A running back has scored at least 15 fantasy points on 35 occasions. Twenty-six, or 74%, came from top-15 positional picks. Fourteen, or 40%, came from the top eight. And six of the 11 games worth 25-plus points came from top-three backs Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson and Jonathan Taylor.

That's not to dissuade zero-RB drafters, who have had success employing the strategy in the past and will probably fare better in the coming weeks as injuries and role changes take hold at the position. Besides, you've got the team you've got at this point, so you need to make the best of it.

Running back has been a particular focus of a couple of my teams this and last week, including in the Vampire league specifically, where the position's ho-hum stats have dug me a 0-3 hole. A pair of backfields that are not the altogether-too-obvious Miami Dolphins -- new leading man Ollie Gordon II was predictably the No. 1 free agent pickup overnight -- have my attention:

New York Jets: It's Braelon Allen, not Gordon, who was my primary focus on the pickups front, after news that usual starter Breece Hall's thigh injury late in Week 3 is a week-to-week, rather than day-to-day, injury. A big, powerful back, Allen might share rushing work with Isaiah Davis while Hall heals, but Allen is a capable fill-in starter with a good matchup in Week 4 (@CHI). I'm anticipating 12-15 carries and top odds on any goal-line carries, and that'd be a pretty good find off free agency for those seeking running back help (which should really be everyone).

Seattle Seahawks: Jadarian Price's fumbling problem is clearly an issue, as it's rare to see a first-round draft pick and Week 1 starter benched three games into his NFL career. Price's lost fumbles in back-to-back games -- 13 carries apart -- got him sidelined for much of Week 3, though Emanuel Wilson didn't do much in Price's stead (1.4 FPTS, 1.6 YPC) after having decent garbage-time stats in Week 2. But then there's Zach Charbonnet, who has one more game to miss while on the PUP list but is eligible to have his practice window opened, something that could happen in the coming days. All indications are that Charbonnet will be ready to play during the season's first half, and if he's back by mid-October, he'd at least be returning at the right time to swiftly reclaim the lion's share of the rushing work. And with all the injuries thus far, fantasy managers might not have been able to keep an IL slot available while waiting for him. If you've got one freed up and he's available in your league, Charbonnet is a worthy stash.

Sept. 29: Case Keenum to the Monday night rescue

By Michael F. Florio

Case Keenum was the star of the show on "Monday Night Football," emerging from third on the Bears' QB depth chart in Week 2 to make the Week 3 start, his first since Dec. 24, 2023. He threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns, completing 71% of his passes. He also added six rushing yards and a touchdown. He finished with 24.48 fantasy points, meaning he has more in one game than Drake Maye does on the season (21.6).

Keenum could be in line to start again in Week 4, and would be in play in superflex leagues against a Jets secondary that has been tough to pass on this season. Tyson Bagent would be the other Bears option while Caleb Williams recovers from his hamstring injury.

Kalif Raymond led the Bears in receiving yards for the second time in three weeks. He and Luther Burden III have been the Bears' top two target-getters in each game. Through three weeks, he is second on the team in targets. He should be the top WR waiver wire pickup, as he is available in almost 90% of leagues. Burden had a big night of his own, seeing a team-high 11 targets, turning them into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. He also added in a 7-yard run. He leads the Bears in targets and has a 32% red zone target share. Burden is blossoming into the must-start option fantasy managers envisioned during draft season.

Both Colston Loveland and Rome Odunze just missed touchdowns. Loveland dove and was down just short of the goal line at the 1. Meanwhile, Odunze had an open touchdown slip through his hands. In total, Odunze turned six targets into three catches for 44 yards. Loveland finished with four catches for 31 yards on four targets. Both players' fantasy stocks remain down. Loveland is in play just because the lack of high-ceiling options at tight end. Odunze though is purely a flex option that should hit a good amount of benches until we see otherwise.
The Bears did not duplicate the rushing success that they had in 2025, but D'Andre Swift did have himself a nice showing. He played 70% of the snaps with 20 carries for 84 yards. He also caught two of three targets for four yards. While he did not score a touchdown, he was used often in the red zone. Kyle Monangai finished with 10 carries for 31 yards. He is a top insurance back but has had trouble finding standalone value.
It was a tough night for Jalen Hurts and the Eagles offense. The team's best drive was right before the half, where Hurts snapped the ball with one second left on the ticking clock and scored his first rushing touchdown of the season. He finished with 153 yards passing and an interception. He missed four plays while in the medical tent and Andy Dalton threw a goal line interception.
Saquon Barkley played 75% of the snaps and turned 15 carries into 82 yards. He saw two targets, catching one for -2 yards. Barkley has yet to score double-digit fantasy points in a game this season. The Eagles face two tough run defenses in their next two games (Rams, Jaguars) but it opens up after that. The next two weeks are an opportunity to acquire Barkley at a discount.
DeVonta Smith saw eight targets, catching six for 65 yards. Through three weeks, he has a 33% target share and a 48% air yard share. That usage could lead to a fantasy WR1 season. He is the only Eagles pass catcher that can be trusted weekly.
Dontayvion Wicks saw five targets, catching two for 32 yards. He has been the top red zone target for Hurts to start the season. That has him in play as a deep-league flex option. Rookie Makai Lemon is still operating as the WR3, but is starting to be used more. He caught three of four targets for 29 yards. He remains a bench stash.

Sept. 28: Jets, Saints grapple with RB injuries

By Michael F. Florio

New York Jets RB Breece Hall is week-to-week after suffering a quad injury on Sunday, per Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter. Rapoport reported that the injury is not as significant as feared.

That leaves Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis active for the Jets. I would anticipate that Allen, who has been the RB2 behind Hall for the past three years, starts and handles the majority of ground work. Both backs have handled limited volume in their careers, but Allen has been the superior runner of the two. He has a 51% success rate.

Davis is a bit of an explosive runner and has been effective as a pass catcher out of the backfield. While he does not have a touch this season, he has caught 75% of targets in his career and averaged 8.7 yards per reception.

Both Jets backs are worth adding in fantasy as this plays itself out in the coming weeks. Allen will be a flex option in a favorable matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Etienne to miss time with hamstring injury
New Orleans Saints coach Kellen Moore announced Monday that RB Travis Etienne Jr. has a hamstring injury that will force him to miss time. Moore did not reveal a specific timetable.

That leaves the Saints' backfield with Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller. I would expect Kamara to handle the bulk of the passing downs, while the two will likely split the ground work.

Kamara has seen nine carries in each game he has played this season and racked up seven targets. The efficiency is gone, as he has averaged just 2.6 yards per touch. Still, volume keeps him in play as a potential flex option moving forward.

Miller is an option for those deep league players. He is the more efficient runner of the two, but we know the Saints are not going to just hand him the job over Kamara. Miller should see enough carries to be in the flex range in deep leagues. How the goal line work is distributed between the two will be huge for fantasy purposes.

Both are volume dependent flex options, with low floors, in a tough matchup against the Falcons next week.

Sept. 28: QB-depleted Giants trade for J.J. McCarthy, Bucs lose Baker Mayfield

By Eric Karabell

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, is now a member of the New York Giants after they sent a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for his services. In some ways, this is stunning. The Vikings gave up on McCarthy after one terrible season in which he completed only 57.6% of his throws and accrued more interceptions than touchdown passes. He is 23, but the Vikings might or might not be set with their future quarterback depending on how newcomer Kyler Murray performs. Early returns -- for Murray's performance and durability -- are quite mixed.

The Giants are taking a chance on an intriguing prospect even though McCarthy did not play well during his first active season. Then again, the Giants already have an intriguing quarterback prospect in Jaxson Dart, the No. 25 pick in the 2025 draft. Dart remains their future quarterback, but concussions marred his rookie campaign, and this season ended in Week 2 with major tears in his left knee. Nobody knows whether Dart can stay healthy for a full season, which is why this trade makes sense for the Giants.

For fantasy purposes, those who roster Dart in a keeper/dynasty league should already have been quite worried about his future in terms of staying on the field. This trade doesn't necessarily alter that. McCarthy missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury, too. The Giants add another body who, when healthy, needs to prove himself on the field. Dart has done that part already.

As for this season's Giants, veteran backup Jameis Winston seems likely to remain the starting quarterback for as long as he is healthy and competent. He was competent enough Sunday, leading the team to a 12-7 win over the Titans, even though he did little to aid fantasy managers statistically. Winston threw for only 118 yards, albeit in difficult weather conditions, but he avoided turnovers. The Winston who passed for 5,109 yards, 33 touchdowns and 30 interceptions for the 2019 Buccaneers is long gone.

Expect Winston to remain the starter, and assuming the Giants prefer Winston to act cautiously as a passer, merely directing the offense and attempting safe throws, it already impedes the upside for WRs Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields, and TE Isaiah Likely. RB Cam Skattebo earned 23 touches Sunday. His volume should remain high. If McCarthy were to replace Winston, it would not appear to aid Nabers, Fields and others, but that is because we don't know enough about McCarthy. One season proved little.

Still, McCarthy has some value for the rest of the 2026 season, as he becomes next in line to start, and for keeper/dynasty formats. McCarthy is young. Quarterbacks struggle to stay healthy in the NFL. It would not be surprising if McCarthy starts some games this season and plays competently, and who knows, perhaps he'll start next season if Dart is compromised. It is tough to assume McCarthy will perform well. His fantasy value rises a bit after this trade because the Vikings had made it abundantly clear they didn't want him around anymore, but the Giants have a franchise quarterback when healthy. The Vikings did not.

How Mayfield's absence affects the Bucs' offense
Tampa Bay Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield left Sunday's game with a dislocated right thumb injury, and word came Monday that he will miss at least the next three weeks. Mayfield, off to a disappointing start statistically and rostered in 49.4% of ESPN standard leagues, is averaging only 11.7 points per game, a bit behind Cam Ward, Aaron Rodgers and Malik Willis. Mayfield will miss enticing games during the next two weeks versus the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys, and then the Buccaneers face the Pittsburgh Steelers and Carolina Panthers.

Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie from Kansas, assumes the starting role. Fantasy managers should be cautious in their pursuit, including in multi-QB and superflex formats, and we must downgrade wide receivers Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin Jr. and others. Daniels, who spent six seasons with the Jayhawks, enjoyed three seasons with at least 2,000 passing yards and 400 rushing yards, and rushed for 17 touchdowns during those seasons. He is not known for his accuracy or decision-making.

stories.headline: Michael Harris II leads Braves to 3-2 win over Dodgers in Game 2 to tie NLDS
stories.summary: — Michael Harris II tripled and scored the go-ahead run on reliever Kris Bubic's wild pitch in the fifth inning, and the Atlanta Braves beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 3-2 on Sunday night to even the National League Division Series at a game apiece.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Michael Harris II tripled and scored the go-ahead run on reliever Kris Bubic's wild pitch in the fifth inning, and the Atlanta Braves beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 3-2 on Sunday night to even the National League Division Series at a game apiece.


Harris' RBI double to right against reliever Edgardo Henriquez added an insurance run with two outs in the seventh in what turned into a bullpen game for both teams when the Braves chased Dodgers starter Blake Snell after 3 2/3 innings.


Harris also singled in the third, coming up a home run short of hitting for the cycle.


Max Muncy's two-strike, two-out homer off Didier Fuentes pulled the Dodgers to 3-2 in the ninth. Braves closer Raisel Igelsias earned his second save after getting pinch-hitter Josue De Paula to foul out to third to end the game.


Runs were hard to come by after the teams combined for five homers in the Dodgers’ 5-3 victory in Game 1.


After Mookie Betts walked and Shohei Ohtani singled to open the fifth, Atlanta's bullpen retired the next 14 consecutive Dodgers' hitters.


Los Angeles stranded seven runners on base over the first five innings. Ohtani, the four-time MVP, wasn’t a factor for the second straight game, going 1 for 4 with two strikeouts.


The Braves retook the lead, 2-1, on Bubic’s wild pitch after Harris' two-out triple.


Freddie Freeman tied it at 1 on a two-strike solo shot off Braves reliever Grant Holmes in the fourth while facing his former team for the first time in the postseason.


Snell struggled throughout, never finding a rhythm. The two-time Cy Young Award winner threw 90 pitches and only 47 for strikes. He gave up one run and three hits, walked five and struck out five.


Snell needed 27 pitches to get through the first, when he had only three more strikes thrown than balls.


The Braves led 1-0 on Mauricio Dubón’s bases-loaded, two-strike single to shortstop with two outs in the first. Betts made a diving stop, but his throw to first was too late, allowing Ronald Acuña Jr. to score after singling and stealing second.


Ray Kerr started the game for the Braves, who elected to give Chris Sale extra rest ahead of his start in Game 3.


Roki Sasaki, the Dodgers' sixth reliever, loaded the bases in the eighth on a walk, hit by pitch and an intentional walk with one out. Acuña hit into an inning-ending double play.


Up next
After a travel day, Braves LHP Chris Sale starts Game 3 on Tuesday in Atlanta against Dodgers RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto.

stories.headline: Mikael Granlund scores in OT, Cutter Gauthier gets 2 goals in Ducks' 3-2 win over Panthers
stories.summary: — Cutter Gauthier scored two power-play goals and captain Mikael Granlund had a power-play goal 4:14 into overtime, sending the Anaheim Ducks to a 3-2 victory over the Florida Panthers on Sunday night...
stories.body:
ANAHEIM, Calif. -- — Cutter Gauthier scored two power-play goals and captain Mikael Granlund had a power-play goal 4:14 into overtime, sending the Anaheim Ducks to a 3-2 victory over the Florida Panthers on Sunday night and their 11th consecutive win in home openers.


Leo Carlsson had three assists for the Ducks, including the setup for Granlund's winner in front of Jacob Markstrom.


Lukas Dostal made 29 saves for the Ducks, who have won their first two games following last season’s successful run to the second round of the playoffs, ending a seven-year postseason drought.


Gauthier delivered his 12th career multi-goal performance and added an assist on Granlund's winner in his first home game since he signed a six-year, $81 million contract extension last month coming off his 41-goal breakout season.


Brad Marchand tied it with 1:50 left in regulation in his season debut for the Panthers, who lost their second straight. Carter Verhaeghe scored an early goal and Markstrom stopped 18 shots.


Beckett Sennecke drew a tripping penalty on Gustav Forsling midway through overtime, but Florida nearly killed the penalty before Carlsson found Granlund in front for his first goal. Carlsson has five points in his first two games after getting his own $90 million extension.


Gauthier scored from the slot on a power play early in the second off Sennecke's setup. Gauthier had an open net for a hat trick late in the second off another superb pass from Sennecke, but he hit the post — and snapped his stick over his knee in frustration moments later.


Florida failed to score on a late power play when former Panthers forward AJ Greer was sent off for hooking, but Marchand converted a rebound with Markstrom pulled for an extra attacker.


Defenseman Aaron Ekblad was a late scratch for the Panthers, who lost captain Aleksander Barkov to a significant left leg injury last Thursday.


Panthers defenseman Radko Gudas played against the team he captained for the previous two seasons, while Greer played against the team with which he spent the past two seasons, winning a Stanley Cup ring in 2025.


Up next
Panthers: At Los Angeles on Tuesday night.


Ducks: Host Edmonton on Wednesday night.

stories.headline: All eyes on Port's Zak Butters call as trade period opens
stories.summary: The Western Bulldogs and Port Adelaide are locked in conversations over Zak Butters and whether he moves as a free agent or via a trade.
stories.body:
Port Adelaide are yet to decide whether they will accept a compensation pick for Zak Butters or match the Western Bulldogs' free agency offer and force a blockbuster trade for the superstar midfielder.

The trade period opened on Monday with all eyes on the Butters deal, while Hawthorn will attempt to secure both Essendon star Zach Merrett and Gold Coast spearhead Ben King.

The Dogs are yet to lodge restricted free agent paperwork for Butters.

Port can accept band one compensation, which would currently deliver pick No. 5 in this year's draft, or match the Bulldogs' offer and force a trade.

"We're working through all those options at the moment," Port list boss Jason Cripps said.

"Clearly the compo pick is something we're trying to explore the market in terms of what that might give us this year and future years.

"But we've also got the capacity to match and force a trade if we choose to do so.

"So it's just a little bit early, testing the market, working through all those options, but not sure which way we pivot at this stage."

The free agency period ends on Friday, meaning the clock is ticking.

Port are unlikely to force Butters - who had significant interest from battling Richmond - into the draft but Cripps gave the Bulldogs a public warning to pay up.

"We've talked around if we're not given something that we think's fair value for Zak's standing in the game and the posturing of pushing him into the draft and what does that look like?" Cripps said.

"I can say we've had a lot of conversations with (Richmond list boss) Blair Hartley over the journey, we're pretty close. So we want to avoid that.

"We've had enough conversations with the Western Bulldogs for them to have a really clear understanding of what our expectations are, and they're getting to work."

Bulldogs list boss Michael Regan labelled Butters "priority number one and two".

The Dogs could get other clubs involved or move players in the deal.

The AFL already flagged clubs cannot complete side deals to run alongside compensation picks unless the trade stands up on its own.

The Bulldogs and Power explored a deal where Port tall Todd Marshall moved in exchange for two first-round draft picks.

That was knocked on the head by the AFL, frustrating both Regan and Cripps.

Reagan confirmed the Dogs no longer hold interest in Marshall.

Defender Rory Lobb wants to stay while a potential trades for Hawk Finn Maginness will wait until the Butters deal is done.

"I think everyone can understand that Zak Butters is priority number one and two," Regan said.

"And hopefully we're able to get that one sorted out reasonably quickly and get the other boys sorted as well."

Elsewhere, Geelong are targeting Essendon defender Jordan Ridley and St Kilda ruckman Rowan Marshall.

Dumped GWS forward Jesse Hogan was the first trade, moving to his fourth club, Collingwood, for pick No.75.

The trade window wraps up on October 14.

stories.headline: DeWanna Bonner's intense halftime talk sparks Dream in win over Liberty
stories.summary: DeWanna Bonner's fiery halftime message spurred the Dream in their 92-82 win over the Liberty in Game 1 of their series.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- DeWanna Bonner wouldn't elaborate on what she said in the locker room as her Atlanta Dream faced a 40-37 deficit in their semifinal opener versus the New York Liberty. "Maybe after the series," she said in the postgame news conference with a smile.

But the late-season acquisition's fiery halftime message helped spur a third-quarter surge that put Atlanta in the driver's seat for the remainder of Sunday's contest.

The Dream rediscovered their identity after the break, stealing the ball from New York nine times in the third alone and scoring 16 points off those turnovers to help them come away with a 92-82 win and go up 1-0 in the best-of-five series.

"DB got into us at halftime, I'll just say that," guard Jordin Canada smirked. "We knew we didn't play our best in the first half. ... We just weren't being aggressive enough on the defensive end and offensive end.

"We talked about a second-half surge, that the first three minutes of the second half are going to be really important, and so we came out ready to go."

Though the Liberty rallied in the fourth to cut a 16-point deficit to five, they didn't get the requisite stops to pull any closer.

Atlanta is now the only team yet to lose this postseason and has won each playoff game by double figures.

The Dream separated themselves this season with their defense and ball pressure. Rhyne Howard, Canada and Angel Reese ranked Nos. 1-3 in the league in steals, and while Reese secured Defensive Player of the Year, she has said any of the three could have won it -- so much so she wants to get the others' names engraved on the trophy.

Atlanta showed on Sunday why that unit -- which in turn fuels so much of its offense -- has been so elite: Atlanta scored 32 points off turnovers on the afternoon, including 16 in the third quarter alone, with both marks tying WNBA records.

The Liberty took a timeout down three at the 8:04 mark of the third to try to stop the bleeding, but it was to no avail. New York turned the ball over another six times and trailed by 12 before managing to hit a shot from the field.

"They upped their defensive pressure, and I think we were driving into driving lanes and not really creating a good outlet for our teammates," said Sabrina Ionescu, who led the Liberty with 27 points but had five turnovers to one assist. "And so I think we'll go back and watch the film and just understand those points off turnovers really matter, especially on a team that thrives off of it."

Added Breanna Stewart (19 points): "They just kind of raced it down our throats, and we need to be better."

Atlanta had to pull out the win with only 11 minutes from top scorer Allisha Gray, who suffered a left hand injury in the first half and was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Coach Karl Smesko did not have an update on Gray postgame besides saying, "hopefully she'll be OK."

Not only did the Dream's collective defensive effort help make up for Gray's absence, but so did the play of veteran leaders Canada and Bonner. The only two members of the team who have previously won a WNBA championship, the duo combined for 48 points on the night.

Canada -- whom Bonner referred to as the "head of the snake on offense and defense" -- scored 12 of her 25 points in the pivotal third quarter, also finishing with five steals and four assists.

Bonner -- who has played in a league-record 101 playoff games -- came in off the bench to add 23 points, including three 3-pointers, and nine rebounds. The 39-year-old agreed to a contract buyout with the Phoenix Mercury in late August in hopes of joining a contender in what could be her final season.

"I just thought she was exactly what we needed," Smesko said. "Not just because she's a veteran presence and all the experience, because she still plays like she did tonight. That was a huge performance, and when we needed a play, she made it."

Reese, who on Sunday was second behind Canada with four steals, said that Bonner "always challenges us" -- and that she wasn't even smiling postgame, reminding the group that nothing has been achieved yet with just one win under their belts.

Game 2 will be back at State Farm Arena in Atlanta on Wednesday before the series moves to New York for Games 3 [Friday] and, if necessary, 4 [Sunday].

"She keeps us together and keeps us pretty grounded," Reese said. "We can do everything we want [to celebrate] today and then tomorrow having the mindset of going in and playing another one on Wednesday. She keeps us pretty humble."
